author: OmegatoAlpha
quote:
Probably the best game on the Switch 2 right now, and absolutely worth the $60 for a physical copy. The Splatoons gameplay is adapted quite well into a more-single player focused game, and the gadgets you can unlock throughout the game are a blast to use, especially when you tinker with them. The game can also be a challenge sometimes, which can be nice for players who are willing to push themselves far, and there are also difficulty settings to customized your experience. Deep Cut are also a joy in this game, and their abilities, while straightforward, are still fun and satisfying to use, especially when you use their showstopper to clutch a level.

And all this isn't even mentioning the little things in the game. You can operate the crane on the ship to grab crates floating by, something very much appreciated, and there are arcade games to unlock as well! They're quire fun side games to play, and while its difficult to get a good rank on them, they're still fun nonetheless, and the fact that these were included when they had no reason to include them makes it all the better. Modern games can be lacking in these side modes and small things, but recent Nintendo games like Mario Tennis Fever and especially Splatoon Raiders have had more side content in them recently, and I'm all for it. This game absolutely is worth $60, and I seriously do recommend you pick it up if you haven't already. It's one of the biggest highlights in the Switch 2's library,

author: OmegatoAlpha
quote:
Now that the review bombing has long passed, let me write my opinion on this

This game is probably my single favorite Pokemon game of all time, at least gameplay wise. The real-time battle system is well put together, and it's far more engaging than the tired turn-based system that every other game in the series uses. The Mega Designs are good for the most part (except for like, Mega Starmie and Pyroar which are the laziest designs I've ever seen and Mega Raichu Y that just looks like a poorly photoshopped Mega Pikachu), and the holographic visuals are very nice, even if the rest of the games visuals are lackluster with corner cutting noticable, with over-reliance on fading to black and playing a sound effect in place of animation in particular being bothersome. The sound design is also nice, although I do think the variants of Pokemon cries from Legends Arcues are better due to sounding more naturally edited. The Pokemon cries are still as charming as ever despite my gripes with the emotion variants sounding like weirdly distorted versions of the actual cries.

The music is also fantastic, with the general soundtrack being much more memorable than Scarlet and Violet. The plentiful side quests are also fun things to do. Inclusion of a photo mode is also appreciated, even if i wish it had much more filters that looked cooler like Super Mario Odyssey.

So overall? The gameplay is the best Pokemon has ever seen by a landslide, and I had a blast with the game, despite the gripes I do have.

author: OmegatoAlpha
quote:
So basically, the traditional 3 lap races are really fun, and I love the kart design, sticker system, free roam, knockout tour, music, the fun roster, the idea of outfits, and ESPECIALLY the visuals. The routes (or intermissions as theyre called by the community) need some work, mainly heavy nerfs to bagging (which is far too powerful in routes, and is in general a strategy thats lame to everyone involved, whether they're doing it, watching it, or being victim to it), and bagging in general feels cheap and unfair. Tighter boundaries in routes would also help immensely, as I believe the game is too generous on whats considered in bounds on routes.

Another issue is that the online system is awful, and got even worse with the recent update. A lot of people picked random to avoid doing the unpopular route races, as random used to always pick a 3 laps around a track race. However, the update was Nintendo doubling down on an unpopular gameplay style, with random now almost always picking routes. While I dont think routes are inherently flawed and unsalvageable, the decision to restrict online options even more is an awful move, and is a candidate for the top 10 worst updates in gaming history. A simple option to queue for random matchmaking lobbies that only have traditional 3 lap race around a track races would make the online system so much better. However, Nintendo did the exact opposite, and people are rightfully outraged, and some have even gone back to playing Mario Kart 8 Deluxe, which is a pretty bad sign.

Unlocking most characters in this game is also awful, its very similar to Smash 4 custom moves, which is a VERY bad thing. Its basically complete luck on whether you unlock a character, as most need to be unlocked by you being turned into that character by the Kamek item. I don't like the transformation mechanic the item has in general because I don't like being forced to play as a character I didn't pick, even if its temporary, but the fact that you have to rely on these transformations to unlock most characters in the game is awful and means unlocking them all takes so much time and is not fun in the slightest. I would have much prefer the transformation mechanic not be in the game at all and unlocking characters via things like coins or unlocking a new racer every 5-10 or so races. Would also be nice for the enemy drivers like Dry Bones, Rocky Wrench, Pianta, etc. to get outfits as well, since theres a ton of potential there.

I also don't like the roster cuts that were made. I think dropping the Koopalings from the roster was a bad move and I really hope they come back as a DLC pack. Roster itself is solid, although the menu is inflated because for whatever reason the outfits for characters are treated as separate slots on the character select.

Free Roam is pretty basic, but it's fun to drive around the island and do missions along the way. It's also fun to knock things over in free roam. I like the photo mode feature and I'm glad its present in the game, but I really wish there were filters like in Super Mario Odyssey. Odyssey had so many cool filters like NES, SNES, Fisheye, Gameboy, Coin, etc. and I really want to see them in Mario Kart World.

Overall, Mario Kart World IS a good game, however it's held back immensely by several flaws, the biggest of which is the heavy restrictions on online play. Sometimes I just want to play 3 lap races, and I think people should have the option to race only the traditional 3 laps around the track races in random matchmaking if they so chose. But yeah, fun roster, fun gameplay, amazing visuals, nice soundtrack, great kart design. Its just that intermissions need heavy balance changes and the online system really needs to be revamped, as well as some other minor flaws. Since the online and route balance issues are major problems, I can't rank this game any higher than a 7/10. Its a shame because this games fun, I have a good time with it, but this games flaws really hold it back.

- Omega The Rocky Wrench
